comparison: Both evaluate the library construction and validation (C5-C9, C114-C115) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes western blotting validation and design features, while peer reviewers describe it as 'well-designed' with 'nicely controlled data' and 'convincing evidence.' Strong agreement on methodology quality.

OpenEval evaluates lipidomics methodology (C10-C11, C30-C31, C33, C35) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also accept the lipidomics approach, noting 'wide-ranging lipidomics dataset with repeats and SDs.' Both agree on the quality of the lipidomics validation.

OpenEval evaluates C33 (metabolic chasing validation) as SUPPORTED within broader lipidomics claims. Peer reviewers separately acknowledge this as 'nicely controlled data' without specific challenge. Agreement on methodological validation.

OpenEval evaluates NPC1/NPC2 findings (C12, C36-C37) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers acknowledge the study 'confirmed some of the evidence obtained by their own and other research groups in the past.' Both accept these confirmatory findings.

OpenEval evaluates NPC1/NPC2 sphingomyelin accumulation (C38-C45) as SUPPORTED with multiple complementary approaches. Peer reviewers accept these as part of confirmatory evidence. Strong agreement on validation of known phenotypes.

Both evaluate ORP9/ORP11 role in sphingomyelin metabolism (C49-C55) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergent phenotypes and functional assays. Peer reviewers describe this as 'unreported role' with 'compelling new evidence' and 'convincing evidence.' Strong agreement on novel findings.

Both evaluate dimerization findings (C58-C65) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights computational predictions and experimental validation including mitochondrial targeting. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'the authors discovered that ORP9 and ORP11 form a dimer' and describe study as 'well-designed.' Strong agreement.

Both evaluate FFAT motif and VAPA/VAPB interactions (C66-C72, C74) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes co-immunoprecipitation and proximity labeling. Peer reviewers implicitly accept through overall positive assessment. Agreement on mechanistic findings.

Both evaluate localization findings (C75-C79) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes C79 is appropriately presented as hypothesis. Peer reviewers accept localization data as part of mechanistic model without challenge. Agreement on localization supporting dimerization model.

Both evaluate interdependent Golgi localization (C80-C82) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes mislocalization rather than protein instability. Peer reviewers accept as part of overall mechanistic evidence. Agreement on localization findings.

Both evaluate lipid transfer activities (C83-C90) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights in vitro assays and PI(4)P transfer as novel. Peer reviewers acknowledge findings with 'simple take home message that PS traffic to the TGN by ORP9/11 is required.' Agreement on transfer activities despite mechanistic gaps noted by reviewers.

Both evaluate PS transfer in reconstituted contact sites (C91) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes elegant demonstration of functional cooperation. Peer reviewers implicitly accept as part of 'convincing' evidence package. Agreement on functional cooperation.

Both evaluate PS/PI(4)P phenotypes (C95-C99) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes biosensor experiments and rescue specificity. Peer reviewers accept findings as part of evidence for ORP9/ORP11 function. Strong agreement on phospholipid imbalances.

OpenEval evaluates enzymatic activity controls (C100-C103) as SUPPORTED, distinguishing synthetic capacity from substrate delivery. Peer reviewers accept the data but note 'lack of mechanistic understanding' about how PS affects SMS1. Agreement on data quality but divergence on mechanistic clarity.

OpenEval evaluates de novo synthesis defects (C104-C106) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept data but express uncertainty about mechanism, noting 'I still struggle to find any ideas about the aspect of SMS1 function that is being affected.' Agreement on observation but mechanistic gap acknowledged.

OpenEval evaluates Golgi isolation and ceramide delivery findings (C107-C112) as SUPPORTED, calling it 'critical result.' Peer reviewers accept data but maintain UNCERTAIN evaluation due to mechanistic gaps between PS delivery and sphingomyelin synthesis. Agreement on data quality but divergence on sufficiency of mechanistic explanation.

OpenEval evaluates main conclusions (C113, C150-C151) as SUPPORTED, noting mechanism remains 'somewhat indirect.' Peer reviewers accept overall conceptual framework as 'valuable conceptual advancement' while acknowledging mechanistic details remain unclear. Agreement on significance despite mechanistic uncertainties.

Both evaluate PG accumulation claims (C116-C120) with similar assessments. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to speculative mechanism (C120). Peer reviewers accept as SUPPORTED but do not challenge the speculative nature. Minor divergence in evaluation type but agreement that mechanism is untested.

OpenEval evaluates differential severity findings (C121-C124) as SUPPORTED with reasonable interpretation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting 'broader role of hetero-dimerization...is not thoroughly addressed' and compensation by ORP10 remains unresolved. Agreement on observations but divergence on completeness of explanation.

OpenEval evaluates ORP10/ORP11 functional differences (C125-C128) as SUPPORTED while noting mechanistic basis unclear. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, emphasizing that hetero/homo-dimerization impacts 'remain to be fully understood.' Agreement on data but divergence on sufficiency of current understanding.

OpenEval evaluates expression correlation data (C132-C135) as SUPPORTED, noting speculative implications. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating hetero-dimerization role 'is not thoroughly addressed.' Agreement that functional implications remain to be tested.

Both evaluate CERT localization observation (C139-C143) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes hypothesis is plausible but untested. Peer reviewers neither validate nor challenge, viewing it as requiring further investigation. Strong agreement that this represents interesting observation needing validation.

Both evaluate broader conceptual framework (C144-C149) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate presentation of speculative extensions. Peer reviewers view positively as 'valuable conceptual advancement' encouraging further exploration. Agreement on conceptual contribution despite mechanistic uncertainties.

OpenEval evaluates protein domain architecture and EM validation (C56-C57) as SUPPORTED, ruling out gross structural defects. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific structural validation claims.
